findings: HB127 removal instruction 7 and mounting instruction 2 explicitly identify the rear bulkhead as the transmission holding interface. Collision freedom is not proof of attachment.
SNL27 shows two M388 frame holding bolt assemblies, each with one 3/4-inch SAE hexagon nut and one 3/4-inch lock washer. Bolt length and actual receiving geometry are not given here.
SNL205 lists four M390 transmission frame holding screws. The page establishes quantity and identity but not their mounting location, length or role in a jacking/spacing arrangement.
SNL95 lists two M391 outside-bracket support feet, each with one 1-inch jam nut. The prior SNL42 nested outside-bracket composition implies four feet; the quantity conflict remains retained.

The native following-frame lower web projects inside the inspected SNL23 band; the upper web lies 3.606 mm above its nearest band edge under the conditional bearing-based scale. Neither is a machining tolerance.

Both fixed and following frames have unfilled bulkhead gaps. The following frame retains 18.771 mm channel-to-bulkhead and 55.218 mm lower-channel-to-floor gaps. These measurements neither prove intended clearances nor authorize arbitrary packing.
Long MX5 bosses and bracket packing remain approximate. The original cast-wing silhouette discrepancy is not fixed by frame translation.
decision: Use the following-frame hypothesis for subsequent development because it restores original local fit and improves relative source agreement without new collisions.
